protectedReasoning: One non-cancellation failure opens the breaker. Calls are rejected for ten logical units. After cooldown permit at most one concurrent recovery probe. Its failure reopens for another cooldown; its success closes. Cancellation releases a probe and permits a replacement without classifying cancellation as backend failure.

The explicit caller/adapter configuration makes the declared protection checkable from visible inputs: Recovery operations use the supplied cancellation-aware `OptionalWork` adapter. The caller creates one `ManualClock`, constructs the displayed breaker and first runs a scripted immediate non-cancellation failure to open it at time zero. After advancing to the cooldown boundary, it submits three calls before settling any probe. Each probe operation invokes `OptionalWork.open` with the signal passed by the breaker; pending probes settle only on explicit completion, failure or abort, and remove their listeners on settlement. There is no external admission or retry controller. Additional scripts exercise the declared success/failure/cancellation transition rules with immediate scripted outcomes or cancellation-aware pending work.
Protection applies to this declared path and schedule, not arbitrary production workloads.
forbiddenClaims: Production-wide outage, real data loss or traffic scale not established by the supplied synthetic trace.
